candidate_ideas.name: KryptonDB
candidate_ideas.pain: Developers building local offline-first apps must choose between fragile flat files or heavy external database servers.
candidate_ideas.problem: Embedded key-value stores lack native multi-document ACID transactions and rich query capabilities without pulling in bloated relational engines.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency embedded document database engine written in Java 21 featuring a custom JSON-like query parser, a B+Tree on-disk index manager, multi-version concurrency control (MVCC), and a crash-safe write-ahead log.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Embedded systems engineers and local-first application developers
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic integration suite feeding malformed JSON documents, concurrent transaction rollbacks, and simulated disk corruption to verify atomic recovery.

candidate_ideas.name: ApexLang Interpreter
candidate_ideas.pain: Studying language implementation requires navigating massive codebases with complex external build systems and dependencies.
candidate_ideas.problem: Most interpreted language implementations hide memory management details, lexical analysis passes, and stack-frame layout mechanics behind runtime abstractions.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency tree-walk and bytecode interpreter implemented in C11 for a statically-typed expression language, complete with explicit scope resolution, a custom heap allocator, and a mark-and-sweep garbage collector.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Compiler engineers and systems programming educators
candidate_ideas.verification: Automated regression test runner validating syntax errors, lexical edge cases, recursive closure captures, and intentional memory leaks under strict bounds checks.

major_features: Columnar binary file writer with run-length encoding (RLE) and dictionary compression

Volcano iterator model (open/next/close) orchestrating query pipeline execution

Cost-based query optimizer utilizing column statistics histograms for plan selection
Parallel scan coordinator leveraging Java 21 Virtual Threads for concurrent chunk retrieval
Hash-based aggregation engine operating directly on memory-mapped column segments
Dynamic schema evolution engine supporting zero-copy column additions and renames
candidate_ideas.name: TitanQuery
candidate_ideas.pain: Running aggregations locally requires heavy distributed clusters that cannot fit on developer workstations.
candidate_ideas.problem: Traditional disk-based analytics engines struggle with ad-hoc aggregations over massive streams because row-oriented memory layouts cause severe cache misses.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency columnar analytics engine written in Java 21 that implements vectorized query execution, dictionary encoding, run-length compression, and a Volcano-style iterator model over raw binary columnar files.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Data platform architects and analytics engineers
candidate_ideas.verification: Comprehensive test suite verifying numerical overflow handling, malformed compression chunks, mismatched schema joins, and projection boundary errors.

Segmented append-only on-disk log storage with byte-size and time-based rotation
Consumer group coordination engine implementing partition assignment and heartbeats
Explicit message acknowledgment (ACK) and offset tracking persistence loops
Non-blocking TCP network server utilizing Java 21 Selector and SocketChannel APIs
Configurable message retention policies enforcing background segment pruning
Zero-copy file transfer pipeline utilizing NIO FileChannel primitives
Deterministic simulation harness injecting socket delays and packet drops
candidate_ideas.name: NexusStream
candidate_ideas.pain: Developers cannot easily spin up an isolated, deterministic event log broker for integration testing without heavy container overhead.
candidate_ideas.problem: Modern event streaming brokers require complex external dependencies and cluster management tools, making local testing and development cumbersome.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency append-only event log server written in Java 21 featuring a custom binary wire protocol, segmented segment log storage, consumer group offset tracking, and non-blocking TCP socket multiplexing.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Distributed systems engineers and backend developers
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic test harness simulating network packet fragmentation, abrupt client disconnections, offset out-of-bounds requests, and segment rotation limits.

major_features: Inverted index builder supporting positional postings lists for exact phrase matching
Custom English Porter stemmer and tokenizer enforcing strict word normalization
Sparse BM25 scoring engine calculating term frequency and inverse document frequency
Boolean query parser supporting nested AND, OR, and NOT operator trees
On-disk binary serialization layout incorporating CRC32 integrity verification
Incremental document update and deletion pipeline maintaining index consistency
Wildcard and prefix term expansion engine querying dictionary terms efficiently
Snippet extraction highlighter generating contextual summaries around matched terms
candidate_ideas.name: SpectraIndex
candidate_ideas.pain: Lightweight keyword search libraries lack phrase matching, positional indexing, and advanced relevance scoring algorithms.
candidate_ideas.problem: Embedding full-text search capabilities into local applications usually requires heavy external search daemons that complicate distribution and packaging.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency full-text search engine written in Python 3.12 that builds inverted indexes with positional postings lists, implements a custom Porter stemmer, and calculates BM25 relevance scores.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Search engineers and local-first software architects
candidate_ideas.verification: Unit test suite testing empty queries, malformed boolean nesting, special character escaping, and incremental document updates without index corruption.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; the factory does not claim live market research or verified market demand.

A passing systems release proves the generated source compiled or byte-compiled and its factory-required unit/integration suites passed; it does not by itself prove production-scale reliability, security certification, or benchmark superiority.
Generated systems projects intentionally use standard-library-only Java 21, C11, or Python 3.12 profiles so validation can be deterministic and does not depend on unverifiable third-party packages.

Hard projects are scoped implementations of real mechanisms, not claims of complete compatibility with Redis, full SQL standards, industrial compilers, or frontier machine-learning systems unless the tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate that scope.
